events.title: Council updates the Street Maintenance and Rehabilitation Policy and adopts the Five-Year Paving Plan (Equity Alternative)

decision.value: Adopted Resolution No. 70,204-N.S. updating the Street Maintenance and Rehabilitation Policy and the Five-Year Paving Plan "Equity Alternative", amended to approve the first three years of the plan, with the condition that its criteria would not govern funds from potential future ballot measures; staff to return in January 2024.

citations.quote: Paving Plan Equity Alternative amended to approve the first three years of the plan

money.needed: The annotated agenda states no amount; the plan's funding levels are in the staff report, to collect.

purpose.needed: Policy goals and the plan's expected results

alternatives.value: Documented at the time: the Public Works Commission recommended a different plan, version 12A ("Arterial Alternative"), and a Councilmember-authored policy update was also on the agenda. Council adopted the Equity Alternative instead.

actual.needed: Paving delivered under this plan, by year

outcomes.needed: Whether the January 2024 policy update came back as directed

outstanding.needed: No financial commitment stated in the record we hold.

uncertainties: The record does not list individual names for "All Ayes" votes.

events.title: Council commits $8 million a year more of General Fund money to street maintenance

decision.value: Adopted Resolution No. 70,456-N.S., a fiscal policy allocating $8 million a year from the General Fund to street maintenance on top of the existing $7.3 million, $15.3 million in all, adjusted for inflation. It may be suspended in a year Council draws $1 million or more from the Stabilization Reserve to adopt a budget, or by a two-thirds vote of Council.

citations.quote: existing General Fund street paving budget of $7.3 million
a two-thirds vote of the City Council
allocate $8 million annually in General Fund monies for street maintenance

purpose.value: "This policy is needed to ensure that deferred street maintenance is supported by an ongoing adequate General Fund contribution."

citations.quote: ensure that deferred street maintenance is supported by an

alternatives.value: Documented at the time: the policy itself sets two ways to suspend it (a Stabilization Reserve draw of $1 million or more, or a two-thirds vote). No alternative funding level was voted on in the record we hold.

citations.quote: a two-thirds vote of the City Council

actual.needed: General Fund paving appropriations and actual expenditures each year since FY2023

outcomes.value: City staff (July 2026): about 29.4 centerline miles paved in FY2024-FY2026, against a historical average of about 2 to 3 miles a year, an acceleration staff attribute to "the commitment of additional General Fund resources in 2022". This is the City's attribution, not a BeTH finding.

citations.quote: This acceleration was made possible by the commitment of additional General Fund

outstanding.value: Carried into Measure FF: voters made the $15.3 million (inflation-adjusted) non-FF street budget a condition of collecting the tax (BMC 7.11.030(B)).

uncertainties: Whether every year since FY2023 met the $15.3 million (adjusted) level is not yet established.
The record does not list individual names for "All Ayes" votes; two members arrived after roll call and the agenda does not say whether they were present for this item.

events.title: Council places a $650 million housing and infrastructure bond on the November 2022 ballot

decision.value: Adopted Resolution No. 70,492-N.S. placing a $650 million general obligation bond "to create affordable housing; repair streets and sidewalks; underground utilities; and enhance buildings, infrastructure, and safety" on the November 8, 2022 ballot.

citations.quote: Ayes - Kesarwani, Taplin, Bartlett, Harrison, Hahn, Wengraf, Robinson, Arreguin; Noes - None; Abstain - None; Absent - Droste
the issuance of $650 million in general obligation bonds

purpose.value: Affordable housing, climate resiliency, wildfire protection and other public infrastructure, including street and sidewalk repair.

alternatives.value: Documented at the time: the recommendation offered $600 million or $650 million; the July 26, 2022 item had proposed $300 million before Council asked for a revised measure.

citations.quote: obligation bond in the amount of either $600 million or $650 million

actual.needed: A ballot authorization is not an expenditure.

outcomes.needed: November 8, 2022 election result for this measure
outcomes.where_to_look: Alameda County Registrar of Voters; Council resolution confirming results

uncertainties: The election result is not yet in BeTH's records.

events.title: Council authorizes a $5.5 million internal loan for Marina dock replacement

decision.value: Adopted Resolution No. 70,997-N.S. authorizing an internal loan of $5.5 million from the Workers' Compensation Fund, to be repaid from waterfront hotel tax starting in FY2025.

citations.quote: authorizes an internal loan of $5.5M from the Workers Compensation Fund
Ayes - Kesarwani, Taplin, Bartlett, Hahn, Wengraf, Robinson, Humbert, Arreguin; Noes - None; Abstain - None; Absent - Harrison

value.basis: loan authorization (not revenue, not an expenditure)

purpose.value: Replace the Marina's D and E docks.

citations.quote: $5.5M Loan for D and E Dock Project In Berkeley Marina

alternatives.value: Documented at the time: amend the existing $5.5 million State boating loan under one of four options, or borrow internally. Council chose the internal loan.

citations.quote: execute an Amendment to the existing $5.5M Loan

actual.value: The FY2024 audit records $5,500,000 leaving the Workers' Compensation Fund to the General Fund; the Marina Fund recorded no transfer in. See the Ask BeTH Marina answer.

outstanding.needed: Loan balance and repayments from waterfront hotel tax

uncertainties: Whether the loan reached the Marina Fund, and whether repayment has begun, is unresolved.

events.title: Council adopts the Five-Year Street Rehabilitation Plan, FY2024-2028, after a competing motion fails

decision.value: Adopted Resolution No. 71,120-N.S. adopting the staff plan with Milvia Street (Hearst to Rose) added and the Hopkins Street segments to be completed with Measure T1 funds by the end of FY2027; green infrastructure and holdover-list questions referred to committee.

value.text: Adopt the plan with Milvia added, add Hopkins Street (The Alameda to Gilman) to the FY2025 list, refer green infrastructure and holdover issues to committee, and direct a parking management analysis around the Hopkins corridor.

citations.quote: Ayes - Bartlett, Hahn, Wengraf, Arreguin; Noes - Kesarwani, Taplin, Harrison, Robinson, Humbert

money.needed: Plan funding by year and source

alternatives.value: Documented at the time: the Hahn/Wengraf motion (below), which failed 4-5.

actual.value: City staff report centerline miles paved: 10.7 in FY2024 and 8.4 in FY2025; 10.3 projected for FY2026. Some streets were deferred to coordinate with Claremont, Oxford and Telegraph projects.

citations.quote: Several streets from the FY 2024-2028 plan have been deferred

outcomes.needed: Whether the Hopkins segments are on track for FY2027

outstanding.value: Hopkins Street segments to be completed with Measure T1 funds by the end of FY2027.

citations.quote: complete the Hopkins Street segments with Measure T1 funds by the end of FY 2027

events.title: Council adopts the Five-Year Street Rehabilitation and Measure FF plans, FY2027-2031

decision.value: Adopted Resolution No. 72,377-N.S. adopting both five-year plans, noting several transportation studies as preliminary Measure FF safety projects subject to the SAFE STREETS oversight committee and Council.

purpose.value: City projection: the paving plan plus Measure FF raises citywide PCI to about 62 by 2038; neither scenario reaches 70 within 12 years.

citations.quote: the citywide PCI is projected to improve to approximately 62 by 2038

alternatives.value: Documented at the time: the City modeled funding scenarios and two ways of choosing Measure FF streets (PCI below 50 versus cost-effectiveness).

outstanding.value: Five years of planned paving and Measure FF projects; see the Ask BeTH street pages.
outstanding.note: Plan totals and street lists are cited in the Ask BeTH street answers.

uncertainties: The record does not list individual names for "All Ayes" votes.
